newsitem.title: NORWAY: SOCCER-SIMONE HAT-TRICK PUTS MILAN'S CAMPAIGN BACK ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SIMONE HAT-TRICK PUTS MILAN'S CAMPAIGN BACK ON TRACK.

text.p: A hat-trick from striker Marco Simone steered AC Milan's European campaign back on track on Wednesday as the Italian champions thrashed Norway's Rosenborg Trondheim 4-1.

A three-goal burst from the 27-year-old Simone -- his white boots flashing around sluggish defenders who looked as though they had forgotten to put anti-freeze in their engines -- in the first 25 minutes sank any hopes the Norwegians had of recording their second Group D victory.

Simone and majestic Liberian striker George Weah wove a magical Milanese spell around the frozen Norwegians with an impressive display of one-touch football and running off the ball that left even the partisan crown applauding.

"I never thought we would get this kind of result," said Milan's Uruguayan coach Oscar Tabarez, saying Simone's performance justified the faith he has shown in him over the legendary Roberto Baggio, who began Wednesday's game on the bench.
"We deserved our victory," Tabarez added, relieved at a champions league victory after the shock 3-2 defeat at the hands of Porto two weeks ago.
None of the 20,849 crowd disputed the Italian victory, which could have been twice as big. Simone alone had three chances saved by the Rosenborg goalkeeper's fingertips.
The match could not have started better for the Italians, playing at one of the most northerly venues in European soccer competition.

Milan had already split the Rosenborg defence wide open once when Dutch midfielder Edgar Davids pierced the Norwegian back four for Simone to glide through into the penalty box and slot home his first goal after just six minutes.
With Simone and Weah beginning to link up supremely, the hat-trick scorer saw one chance palmed wide by Rosenborg keeper Joern Jamtfall before the home team scored against the run of play.
The Milan defence looked shaky on the rare occasions it was pressed in the first half and striker Trond Egil Soltvedt thumped home a 15-metre volley from a tight angle to equalise in the 16th minute.
However that was the last moment of joy for the partisan home crowd.
Simone, wearing black gloves to ward off the freezing temperatures, produced two minutes of magic to record his hat-trick.
After 23 minutes he tantalised three Norwegian defenders before cheekily side-footing the ball to the right of Jamtfall to make the score 2-1.
Almost directly from the kick off Yugoslav striker Dejan Savicevic's cross floated gently to the unmarked Simone, whose far-post header was inch perfect and put the Italian champions 3-1 up.

The visitors tormented the hapless Norwegians for the rest of the first half, with Simone a whisker away from scoring two more and Weah -- enjoying playing just behind the darting Simone -- creating several more chances.

After 10 minutes of the second half, Simone unselfishly took several Norwegian defenders with him as he launched a powerful diagonal run, releasing Weah at the last moment for the Liberian to slide the ball past the Norwegian keeper.
Simone, his virtual single-handed destruction of Rosenborg completed, left the field after 73 minutes, leaving the legendary Roberto Baggio just 17 minutes to try to make an impression.
However the only impression he left was of having difficulty teaming up with Weah.

Instead it was Davids, with a number of probing runs through the Norwegian defence, who left the most powerful impression of the second half although he was unable to profit from any of his chances and an embarrassingly open Rosenborg defence.
French central defender Marcel Desailly calmed his back four down in the second half after a hesitant first 45 minutes, introducing authority and firmness to cope with the modest Norwegian attacks.
Teams:

Rosenborg: 1-Joern Jamtfall; 9-Karl-Petter Loeken, 3-Erik Hoftun, 4- Bjoern Otto Bragstad (7-Tom Staurvik, 34th), 5-Staale Stensaas; 6-Roar Strand (14-Vegard Heggem, 81st), 8-Bent Skammelsrud (captain), 20-Trond Egil Soltvedt; 11-Jahn Ivar Jakobsen (18-Bjoern Kvarme, 77th), 10- Harald Brattbakk, 16-Steffen Iversen

AC Milan: 1-Sebastiano Rossi; 2-Christian Panucci, 11-Alessandro Costacurta, 8-Marcel Desailly, 3-Paolo Maldini, 22-Edgar Davids, 4-Demetrio Albertini, 15-Massimo Ambrosini, 10-Dejan Savicevic (24-Stefano Eranio, 42nd); 9-George Weah, 23-Marco Simone (18-Roberto Baggio 73rd).
